pl-l2d27c7-d1e108.summary: Explains that when good merits are said to be from grace, grace means not the giving grace, God, which would be no great thing since all is from him, but grace freely given, which prevents the will. Saying merits are from grace alone does not exclude free choice, since no merit is without it; rather, grace is the principal cause, rousing and healing free choice and helping the will to be good.
claims: Grace is the principal cause of merit.

pl-l2d27c7.summary: Explains that when good merits are said to begin from grace, grace means not the giver, God, which would be trivial since all is from him, but grace freely given, which prevents the will. Saying merits come from grace alone does not exclude free choice, since no merit is without it; rather the chief causal role in meriting belongs to grace, which rouses and heals free choice and helps the will to be good.
claims: Grace here means grace freely given, not God the giver.
Good merits begin from grace freely given.
No merit is without free choice.
Grace is the principal cause of good merits.
